questions.prompt: Choose the model answer: A rising-edge D flip-flop initially has Q=0. D changes 0→1 between edges, then 1→0 just before the next rising edge. What is Q immediately after that edge? Justify.
questions.answer: Q=0. The flip-flop samples D at the rising edge (D=0 at that instant); an earlier pulse between clock edges is not stored.

blocks.title: Key vocabulary
items: clock speed — Number of processor clock cycles each second.
cache — Small, fast memory that reduces some main-memory accesses.
pipeline — Overlap stages of several instructions.
hazard — Dependency or uncertainty disrupting smooth pipelining.
throughput — Amount of work completed in a given time.

blocks.title: Different performance factors
blocks.text: Clock speed indicates cycles per second; multiple cores can execute independent work; cache reduces some slower-memory access.

blocks.title: Overlap pipeline stages
blocks.text: Without overlap, three three-stage instructions need nine stage slots; an ideal pipeline finishes them by the fifth cycle.

blocks.title: Account for hazards
blocks.text: Branches, data dependencies and waiting for memory may cause stalls or pipeline flushing; pipelining does not make every instruction individually three times faster.

blocks.text: Cycle 1 fetch I1. In cycle 2 decode I1 while fetching I2.

blocks.title: Worked example · Explain and check
blocks.text: Cycle 3 executes I1 and decodes I2; I2 executes in cycle 4.
